correctness.rationale: An edge is initially observed in the line graph exactly when it meets the set T of selected endpoints. An observed edge wholly in T has no unobserved neighbor, while an observed boundary edge xy with y outside T has exactly deg(G[V\T],y) unobserved neighbors. Since nonempty S meets at least two parts, every uncovered vertex has an observed boundary edge to a covered vertex in a different part. The induced uncovered complete multipartite graph is either edgeless, a star (every edge can be forced simultaneously at a leaf), or of minimum degree at least two (no force can begin). For fixed uncovered counts, choose the uncovered labels, then apply inclusion–exclusion over missed labels among the remaining vertices; the empty remaining vertex set contributes zero after subtracting the empty selection. This verifies both size and round exponents, with zero measured after initial domination. An independent direct propagation enumeration agreed coefficientwise with the bivariate formula on (1,1,2), (1,2,3), (2,2,2), (1,1,1,3), and separately on the bipartite example (3,3).
residual_risks: The enumeration is finite corroboration. It is not used in place of the general residual-degree and inclusion–exclusion proofs.

value.rationale: Two selected sets of the same size can require different propagation effort. The exact joint distribution, valid for arbitrary mixed part sizes, identifies precisely when propagation can start and why it then terminates in one round; it is more informative than the minimum number or ordinary domination polynomial. The residual classification isolates the obstruction from three occupied uncovered parts, absent in the rook case.
residual_risks: The result makes no computational-efficiency claim and does not analyze forcing rules other than ordinary one-neighbor power domination.
